item.title: Florida is sinking 3 million pounds of repurposed concrete culverts off Destin-Fort Walton Beach
item.description: In an innovative approach, old concrete pipes are being repurposed as artificial reefs in the Gulf of Mexico. This initiative will create three new underwater habitats near Destin-Fort Walton Beach. These structures offer vital shelter for various marine species and bolster local fisheries. Additionally, this project enhances Florida's Coastal Corridor program by linking essential marine ecosystems, benefiting charter boats, fishermen, and scuba divers alike.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Italy to limit foreign students, ban burqa and hijab in schools
item.description: In a bold move, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni unveiled new regulations for schools, prohibiting face coverings such as burqas and niqabs in classrooms. The initiative also sets a limit on foreign students per class and requires parents of foreign students to learn Italian, promoting integration and ensuring that Italian children feel at home, rather than a minority in their own schools.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: ‘Such a cancerous influence’: Diana’s brother on Harry, Meghan’s media scrutiny
item.description: Earl Charles Spencer expresses concern that Prince Harry and Meghan are enduring media scrutiny akin to what his sister, Princess Diana, experienced. He emphasizes the importance of learning from Diana's tragic encounters with the paparazzi, which ultimately led to her untimely death in a Paris car crash. The couple's decision to step back from royal duties was largely influenced by their struggles with media negativity.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In 2022, Adele bought Sylvester Stallone’s 3.5-acre Beverly Park mansion for $58 million; four years...
item.description: In a bold real estate move, Adele bought Sylvester Stallone's stunning Beverly Hills home for $58 million in 2022. Her plans? A total demolition and rebuild of the luxurious estate, while preserving the iconic Rocky Balboa bronze statue that adds a unique flair to the deal. With a modern design featuring expansive glass panels, this renovation is set to reshape the property over the next few years.

item.title: ‘Path of deception closed’: Iran vows ‘no limits’ in retaliation if US attacks
item.description: Iran has issued a stern warning, promising unlimited retaliation and a decisive conflict if the US attacks or dismisses its demands. Through Qatari mediators, Tehran has proposed seven conditions for a truce to Washington. Officials in Iran stressed that any regional nations supporting the US would be drawn into the conflict. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf reiterated the dual approach of military readiness alongside diplomatic negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Meet Nathan Tan, the 17-year-old Plano teen whose AI air-quality project serves about 1,000 Texans
item.description: A young innovator from Plano has created an AI tool that tracks air pollution in underprivileged neighborhoods. This groundbreaking project not only garnered him a national award with substantial prize money but also offers educational resources and air purification devices to families in need. Moreover, the initiative cultivates young leaders who can adeptly analyze air quality data, tackling environmental disparities and enhancing community health.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 75-year-old Gertrude Abercrombie painting bought for $30 could fetch $250,000
item.description: A Michigan collector paid $30 for Gertrude Abercrombie’s 1951 painting at an estate sale, unaware it had been missing from public view for 75 years. After an archival photograph helped confirm its identity, an expert authenticated the work. Alderman Merriam’s Shells will be auctioned in New York with an estimate of $150,000 to $250,000.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Washington couple’s $50M retreat on Lake Washington lists for $71M
item.description: Dwayne and Terese Clark are selling their Lake Washington estate for seventy-one million dollars. This waterfront compound features two Mediterranean-style residences on two point three acres. The property includes a main house and a separate wellness retreat with pools. They are relocating to Arizona after investing fifty million dollars into the homes. The sale could set a new record for Pacific Northwest residential real estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Trump adds drones, snipers and ammunition to plans for Washington triumphal arch
item.description: US President Trump announced plans to transform a proposed triumphal arch into a military complex. This new facility will house and deploy drones and snipers for national security. The structure is planned near Arlington Memorial Bridge, adjacent to the cemetery. Veterans have filed lawsuits challenging the arch's construction and sightline disruption. The Federal Aviation Administration has cleared aviation concerns for the proposed arch.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: California funds 15 projects with $44 million to protect forests, desert and Tribal land
item.description: California has approved $43.868 million for 15 conservation projects across 11 counties. The funding will help protect 14,177 acres of forest and salmon habitat, conserve 1,093 Mojave Desert acres, restore streams and meadows, and acquire an 80-acre Tribal property for ecological restoration and training.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 17-year-old turns her love of photography into a cancer fundraiser
item.description: For over a year, a Brooklyn teenager showcased the allure of Prospect Park in her photographs. The passion project transformed into a community print sale aimed at supporting cancer research for Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. Inspired by her father’s battle with cancer, she cleverly merged creativity and community spirit to make a difference in the fight against the disease.

item.title: Atlanta teacher warned students away from locked 26-acre forest; $3 million may open it
item.description: For years, Atlanta teacher Renette Scott warned students against entering the locked woods outside Therrell High School, unaware that the 26-acre forest was city-owned. After years of community advocacy, Atlanta secured a $2 million state grant and will add $1 million of its own to help turn Falling Water Park into a public park with trails, a lake boardwalk and wildlife education.
